card.name: Cemiplimab (Libtayo) dosing and adverse-reaction text
card.fires_on: Digits and drug-name pieces (LIB, TAYO, UNLOXCYT, WASKYRA) in oncology label text about adverse reactions, discontinuation and dose schedules. Often on a number just before mg or a percentage.

modes.label: Numbers in doses and rates
modes.description: A digit inside a dose, grade, or percentage in a dosing line or adverse-reaction statistic.
modes.example: Adults with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (laBCC) or metastatic BCC (mBCC) 3<<5>>0 mg every

modes.label: Inside the brand name
modes.description: Pieces of a brand name such as LIBTAYO or a word right before it, in discontinuation or withholding statements.
modes.example: Type 1 diabetes mellitus led to withholding of LIBT<<AY>>O in 0.1% of

modes.label: Grade and week lists
modes.description: Spaces or commas inside grade labels or lists of dosing weeks.
modes.example: The recommended dosage is 320 mg by subcutaneous injection at Weeks 0, 2<<,>> 4, 6, 8

card.writes: Promoted tokens are mostly Chinese words meaning carry, hold or rate, so there is no clear link to English label text.
card.plain: It lights up on numbers and brand-name pieces in cancer-drug labels, especially for LIBTAYO dosing and side-effect rates.
